title: Entitlement backlog with a flat replica count
telemetry: Protected synthetic packet combines Kubernetes events and sanitized HorizontalPodAutoscaler status for cluster entitlement-processing (the k8s_cluster events log), supplied GKE console metadata, a Cloud Monitoring Pub/Sub subscription series and labelled platform, application and ledger owner observations. Admitted gcloud logging read returns the packet; it does not grant kubectl, cluster credentials, node access or direct external-metrics API reads. The declared GKE version is an illustrative synthetic snapshot, not a current supported-version claim.
owner: Tamsin, Entitlements on-call, owns the investigation. Bao, the entitlement application owner, owns entitlement-worker and proposes its HorizontalPodAutoscaler spec; Solveig, the GKE platform owner, owns the cluster's custom-metrics adapter and approves HPA replica-limit changes; Ifeoma, the entitlement-ledger owner, owns the ledger entitlement-worker writes to and its connection budget; the messaging owner supplies the Pub/Sub subscription series. ITO coordinates the existing TLC and change approvals.
task: Tamsin has asked you to investigate why the entitlement-events backlog keeps growing while entitlement-worker in cluster entitlement-processing, namespace entitlements, project synthetic-entitlements-prod, us-central1, has not added replicas. Review the available observations for 2026-10-14 09:30-10:40 UTC and return a bounded technical finding that separates what is measured, what the autoscaler intends and the capacity actually running, with evidence, remaining unknowns and the next useful check with its owner. Continue through the existing TLC. No change is approved.

sources.claim: The HPA computes desiredReplicas = ceil[currentReplicas x (currentMetricValue / desiredMetricValue)], skips scaling within a default 0.1 tolerance, averages AverageValue targets across Pods (external and object metrics count Running and Ready Pods), and takes the largest proposal across metrics. If any metric cannot be converted into a replica count, for example after a metrics-API fetch error, and the readable metrics suggest scaling down, scaling is skipped; it can still scale up. Default scale-up allows 100% or 4 Pods per 15 s, and the control loop runs every 15 s by default.

autoscaling/v2 sets AbleToScale, ScalingActive and ScalingLimited conditions; ScalingActive False generally indicates problems fetching metrics, and ScalingLimited indicates the desired scale was capped by the HPA's minimum or maximum. External metrics sum the matched series and support Value and AverageValue targets. ValidMetricFound and DesiredWithinRange appear in the documented example; TooManyReplicas and FailedComputeMetricsReplicas are upstream controller strings (kubernetes/kubernetes pkg/controller/podautoscaler/horizontal.go, release-1.33) not documented on these pages, so the case grades the condition status and the replica bound, not reason or message wording.

The custom/external metrics pipeline runs from the HPA controller through the metrics API and a metrics adapter such as custom-metrics-stackdriver-adapter to a source such as Cloud Monitoring; a broken pipeline shows the metric as <unknown> with FailedGetExternalMetric events, and the HPA conservatively refuses to scale down when a metric is unavailable. ScalingLimited shows the HPA wants to scale but is capped by minReplicas or maxReplicas. HPA events are found in Cloud Logging with resource.type k8s_cluster, logName events and involvedObject kind HorizontalPodAutoscaler.

The Custom Metrics Stackdriver Adapter runs as Kubernetes service account custom-metrics-stackdriver-adapter in namespace custom-metrics and, with Workload Identity Federation, is granted roles/monitoring.viewer. A Pub/Sub HPA uses external metric pubsub.googleapis.com|subscription|num_undelivered_messages with selector resource.labels.subscription_id and an AverageValue target. The fixture uses this adapter path rather than GKE's newer managed metrics adapter; the adapter's internal failure mode in variant A is deliberately left unknown.

Pub/Sub subscription/num_undelivered_messages (backlog) and subscription/oldest_unacked_message_age are pubsub_subscription gauges sampled every 60 seconds and not visible for up to 120 seconds after sampling, which sets the packet's series cutoff and why the HPA's 10:35 reading can match the 10:33 sample.

k8s_cluster uses labels project_id, location and cluster_name, which the declared export filter uses. The HPA status snapshot, adapter, ledger and subscription records are labelled owner observations compiled into the packet, not native event log entries.

a.conclusion: Since 09:41:15 UTC the HPA cannot read its Pub/Sub backlog metric: ScalingActive=False with reason FailedGetExternalMetric, the external value reads <unknown>, and FailedGetExternalMetric and FailedComputeMetricsReplicas warnings repeat. CPU alone (34% against a 70% target) proposes ceil(8 x 34/70) = 4 replicas, a scale-down the HPA skips while a metric is unreadable, so it keeps the existing 8 replicas, well below maxReplicas 24 with ScalingLimited=False. The backlog is still recorded in Cloud Monitoring, so the measurement path between the source and the HPA is broken; it began three minutes after the 09:38 adapter rollout, but the adapter-side cause is not established. The 8 Pods are healthy at their usual per-Pod rate; capacity is short because the count never grew.
next_checks: Solveig, the GKE platform owner, checks the custom-metrics-stackdriver-adapter rolled out under CHG-7342: its logs, the external.metrics.k8s.io APIService and the adapter's Cloud Monitoring read access, and lists other HPAs on external metrics that report the same condition.

Bao and Solveig decide how to restore the measurement through ITO's change approval; Ifeoma confirms entitlement-ledger headroom first, because once the metric is readable the backlog implies about 75-80 replicas (75 on the 10:33 sample, 80 on the 10:35 sample) and the HPA would scale toward maxReplicas 24.
Tamsin reports ScalingActive, desired and ready replicas, backlog and oldest unacked age on the TLC past the 10:35 cutoff; one improved sample is not recovery.
unsupported: Calling the HPA capped at its maximum or recommending a higher maxReplicas; ScalingLimited is False and maxReplicas is 24.
Concluding that demand is low or that CPU-based sizing is correct because CPU is 34%; the backlog metric is unreadable, not low.
Manually scaling the Deployment, editing HPA min/max or metrics, or redeploying or rolling back the adapter as an applied or approved fix; running kubectl or requesting cluster credentials.
Asserting the adapter's internal cause (version, identity or API registration) from timing alone, or blaming node capacity, quota or unhealthy Pods.
unknowns: Why external metric reads fail after the 09:38 adapter rollout.
Whether other HPAs in the cluster that use external metrics are affected.
Entitlement-ledger headroom for more writers and how fast the backlog drains once scaling resumes.
State after the 10:35 snapshot and series cutoff.

b.conclusion: The HPA reads its metrics: ScalingActive=True with reason ValidMetricFound, an external average of 4,675 per Pod against a 500 target (37,400 total, the 10:33 backlog sample) and CPU 34%. The backlog implies ceil(8 x 4,675/500) = ceil(74.8) = 75 replicas, and the latest 10:35 backlog sample (39,800) gives 80; either is far above maxReplicas 8, so ScalingLimited=True since 10:08 and the Deployment holds at its maximum. The supported mechanism is valid demand above the configured replica ceiling, which CR-2209 set to keep ledger connections (96 of 100) within Ifeoma's budget. The measurement path works, no Warning events appear and the 8 Pods are healthy at their usual per-Pod rate.
next_checks: Ifeoma, the entitlement-ledger owner, states current connection usage and whether more writers are safe, because the 8-replica ceiling encodes the ledger's writer budget.
Tamsin asks the publishing owner whether the 6,000-per-minute surge since 10:05 is expected and how long it lasts; at 8 Pods the backlog grows by about 1,200 per minute and does not drain.

Bao proposes, and Solveig approves through ITO, a bounded option within confirmed ledger headroom or an accepted delay; Tamsin watches ScalingLimited, backlog and oldest unacked age on the TLC past the 10:35 cutoff.
unsupported: Blaming a broken metrics adapter or unreadable metric, or redeploying the adapter; ScalingActive is True and the external value is read.
Raising maxReplicas, manually scaling or editing the HPA as an applied or approved fix without the ledger owner's headroom check and change approval.
Attributing the hold to node capacity, Pending Pods, quota or the cluster autoscaler; all 8 Pods run and the cap is the HPA spec.
Calling the workers unhealthy or a release regression; Pods are Ready with an unchanged per-Pod rate and no rollout since 2026-10-12.
unknowns: Whether the publish surge is expected and how long it continues.
State after the 10:35 snapshot and series cutoff.
